rationale: PINS the placeholder-name removal for UNNAMED interface members. `interface Event<T> { (listener): Disposable }` is a CALL SIGNATURE and `interface Factory { new (seed): Disposable }` is a CONSTRUCT SIGNATURE; TypeScript writes no name for either. The analyzer used to publish a Method symbol named `(call)` and a Constructor named `(new)`, which put the string `(call)` into the symbol table and `contains Event -> (call)` into the graph - an endpoint no index can join, and one name shared by every callable interface in the codebase. The forbids below are the regression pins: neither the symbol nor the edge may come back, and the named member of the same interface must still be contained.

expectRelationships.note: PIN CORRECTED 2026-10-17: expected as `uses`; the duplicate `references` row is forbidden.

forbidRelationships.note: PIN CORRECTED 2026-10-17: the duplicate references row for the same mention must NOT exist.
